newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Caution was the watchword on the South African stock market on Wednesday, as shares clung to weaker levels after earlier being knocked down by futures trading.
Dealers said players were nervous of being caught offsides by futures arbitreurs, who have been blamed for the volatile dealings on the bourse this week.
"People were just sitting on the fence, in case the futures guys came in and knocked the market down like they did yesterday morning and again this morning," a trader said.
Arbitrage activity between the futures and stock market has made for extremely choppy trade, with especially big index-linked stocks gyrating up and down, dealers said.
Better-than-expected half-year results from heavyweight stock SAB, released around 1230 GMT, briefly helped the market off its lows, they said.
But shares soon swivelled lower again, depressed further by the rand losing its nerve and returning to overnight levels after initially striding firmer.
"SAB was briefly better after the results and the indices lifted a little, but then it started to drift again," a trader said.
Offshore selling, albeit not aggressive, was evident during the afternoon. This was met by nervous nibbling at the lower levels by institutions.
At the close the industrial index was 16.1 points weaker at 7,914.1 pushing the overall index down to 6,755.3 -- off 7.3 points on the day.

Amongst stocks, Anglo lost 50 cents to 269 rand, SAB finished the day 50 cents off at 115.25 after climbing to a day's best level of 116.50 soon after its results came out, and Nedcor shed 75 cents or 1.15 percent to 64.75 rand.
On the gold board shares spent a lifeless day hovering just above opening levels as bullion clung to the around the $382 level. The index finished up 10.3 points at 1,711.9.
Kloof upped 125 cents to 43 rand but Loraine lost 30 cents to 14.70.
Traders said stocks would adopt a wait-and-see attitude on Thursday, eyeing activity on the futures market before making any clear decisions on direction.

On the futures market, near-month contracts were steady to weaker in late trading after initially beginning the day on an even keel. Dealers said when contracts dipped to a discount to fair value, arbitrage players bought up futures and sold stock in the spot market.
The December industrial contract was at 7,543/50 from 7,616, the all gold contract little moved at 1,222/25 from 1,223 and the all-share contract unchanged at 6,194.
